title: Spectral Allocation: Why Muon Outperforms Adam, and How to Improve Muon
hook: Probe a transformer's loss landscape direction by direction and a pattern appears: a few volatile directions demand tiny steps, the bulk tolerates far larger. That explains Muon > Adam > SGD.
key_points: The authors decompose momentum buffers into singular directions and measure the loss-optimal step size along each on held-out data.
The resulting profile is anisotropic but stable across batches, training stages, optimisers, and model scales.
A small 'head' of directions sits at the Edge of Stability; the tolerant 'bulk' permits much larger steps.
Muon's uniform scaling underuses the bulk — so SAMuon holds the head at Muon's scale and amplifies the bulk with a static spectral prior.
SAMuon needs 13.3-24.0% fewer tokens than Muon to hit the same validation loss on 124M-1B modded-nanogpt models.
content_html: Orthogonal optimisers like Muon speed up LLM pretraining over Adam, but nobody had a clean account of why. Wu and colleagues probe the loss landscape one singular direction at a time and find a stable, lopsided answer: a few volatile directions can only take tiny steps, while the vast bulk could take far larger ones than anyone is giving them.
extra_html:
The measurement

At checkpoints along real training runs, the authors decompose each momentum buffer into its singular directions and estimate, on held-out data, the step size that would most reduce loss along each one. The resulting spectral profile is strongly anisotropic yet remarkably stable — across batches, across training stages, across optimisers, and across model scales. A volatile "head" operates at the Edge of Stability and supports only small steps; the "bulk" is tolerant and permits substantially larger ones. Reading optimisers through this lens gives a unified story for the observed ordering Muon > Adam > SGD: each allocates step size a little closer to the measured profile than the last.

The fix

The same profile exposes Muon's weakness — uniform scaling leaves the bulk underused. Spectral-Aware Muon (SAMuon) pins the head at Muon's scale and amplifies the bulk using a static spectral prior, via a low-rank randomised SVD; SAMuon-lite approximates this with a two-level rank-one power iteration. Neither adds persistent optimiser state or notable FLOPs at scale, and the idealised exact-whitening versions retain Muon's asymptotic convergence rate under standard assumptions. Across modded-nanogpt models from 124M to 1B parameters, both beat tuned AdamW and Muon baselines in every configuration tested, with SAMuon reaching Muon's validation loss on 13.3-24.0% fewer training tokens. arXiv, 2026.

related.title: Muon: An Optimizer for Hidden Layers
related.hook: Muon orthogonalizes each gradient update before applying it — and trained networks faster than AdamW, the first serious challenger to Adam's reign in years.

related.title: Dion3: Making Muon's Orthogonalization Cheap
related.hook: Muon trains faster than AdamW but pays for it in a cubic-time orthogonalization step. Dion3 attacks that overhead at every layer of the stack — up to 6x faster optimizer steps at matching loss.

related.title: The Loss Doesn't See the Basis, But Adam Does
related.hook: A factored model's loss can't tell which basis you wrote the factors in — but Adam's per-coordinate scaling can. That asymmetry predicts which optimizers keep gradient descent's low-rank bias.

related.title: Why Adam Beats SGD on Transformers: A Hessian Story
related.hook: Adam is the default optimizer for LLMs and nobody could quite say why. This thesis traces it to the shape the Hessian takes during transformer training — and gets Adam-mini out of the explanation.

flashcards.prompt: What is the 'spectral allocation' account of why Muon beats Adam?
flashcards.back_html: Different singular directions of the update tolerate very different step sizes: a volatile head sits at the Edge of Stability, the bulk tolerates much larger steps. Optimisers that allocate step size closer to this profile train faster — Muon closer than Adam, Adam closer than SGD.

flashcards.prompt: What limitation of Muon does the spectral probing analysis expose?

choices.text: Its uniform scaling underuses the tolerant bulk of directions, which could take much larger steps
It takes steps that are far too large along every direction, causing divergence
It requires storing a second momentum buffer, doubling optimiser memory

flashcards.explanation_html: Muon scales all directions uniformly. The measured profile says the bulk could move much further, so SAMuon amplifies the bulk while pinning the head at Muon's scale.

flashcards.prompt: What does SAMuon cost relative to Muon?
flashcards.back_html: Essentially nothing at scale: no persistent extra optimiser state and no notable extra FLOPs. The lite variant (rank-one power iteration) keeps most of the gain at near-zero wall-clock overhead.
